trust_decision.summary: A flow id must be one safe filename token (^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$) before it is turned into a path: decided at the HTTP params schema of the four /api/flows/:id routes and again at the sink in FlowStore.filePath, with only InvalidFlowIdError allowed past the two catches that otherwise swallow errors into 404s.

landing_point.why: The summary names a flow id in @openhop/server; the id arrives from the URL, so the first thing a reader fixes is the GET /api/flows/:id params schema, repeated verbatim for version, PATCH and DELETE at routes.ts:354-360, 412-418 and 516-522. The actual file join is one module away in store.ts.

fix_sites.entry_point: shared guard (new packages/server/src/flow-id.ts) imported by both routes.ts and store.ts, not itself reachable
flowIdParamsSchema reused by all four :id routes
FlowStore.get/save/delete/updateFlow/getVersion (internal store API used by all four routes and by seedBundledExamples)
FlowStore.get (rethrow InvalidFlowIdError instead of returning null)
FlowStore.delete (rethrow InvalidFlowIdError instead of returning false)
server bootstrap CORS hook (see out_of_scope_notes - separate weakness in the same commit, does not reach the traversal flaw)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: FlowStore is internal - packages/server/src/index.ts:6-7 imports it but the package exports only buildApp/startServer (packages/server/package.json:25-32) - and every caller in the tree is one of the four routes already validated by flowIdParamsSchema, so the assertValidFlowId in filePath looks like redundant defence-in-depth that the report does not require.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Two legitimate behaviours sit next to the sink. (1) A genuinely missing flow must still answer 404, so only InvalidFlowIdError may be rethrown out of the catch blocks in get()/delete() - rethrowing everything (or throwing from the guard without a matching catch) turns missing-flow 404s into 500s. (2) Ids containing '-' and '_' must stay valid: the pinned tests fetch '/api/flows/does-not-exist' and expect 404, and seeded ids are 'example-order-flow' / 'example-langgraph' / 'example-openhop', so tightening the rule to the 12-char nanoid alphabet of routes.ts:19-24 breaks every seeded example and the seeding path.

O6_input_shapes: ..%2Fvictim - URL-encoded separator in the :id segment (the shape the published route tests use)
../victim - raw dot-dot segment reaching the store API
any id containing '/', '\\' or '.' plus absolute-path and drive-letter shapes - rejected by the whitelist
example-order-flow / does-not-exist / a_b - dash and underscore ids that must keep passing as 404/200, not 400

O7_producer.where: packages/server/src/routes.ts:181 (nanoid() in the POST handler); second producer packages/server/src/seed-examples.ts:81 (`example-${basename(path,'.yaml')}`)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An upsert/idempotent create that takes the flow id from the body or query (POST /api/flows?id=..., or PUT /api/flows/:id) and passes it to store.save/updateFlow.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The seeder already saves fixed, human-meaningful ids (seed-examples.ts:106-112) and the web UI notes POST /api/flows is non-idempotent (packages/web/src/components/FlowEditorModal.tsx:51), so 'push under a stable name' is a natural next feature - and a params-only pattern never sees this id.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A get-by-meta.path or reload/import route that trusts the `id` field stored inside the YAML (store.ts:93-94 reads file.id from content, not from the filename).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: meta.path is a first-class field (GET /api/flows/tree, routes.ts:277-302) and list() already treats the in-file id as authoritative, so serving a flow by that id after a reload looks like normal code; the params pattern never inspects ids that come off disk.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A directory/prefix parameter on the store (e.g. a per-project flows subdir derived from a user-supplied project name joined to the base dir) reaching the same filePath builder.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: OPENHOP_DATA_DIR is documented as a per-project workspace override (store.ts:24-39), so a per-request data-dir or project segment is a plausible feature that would bypass a single-segment id pattern.

O9_family: path traversal (CWE-22) - unvalidated flow id concatenated into a filesystem path for read, write and delete

O10_build.toolchain: Node ^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0, npm ci, tsc --noEmit, esbuild bundle, vitest
O10_build.project_tests: packages/server/src/routes.test.ts exercises GET/GET version/PATCH/DELETE /api/flows/:id through app.inject with HOME redirected to a tmpdir; packages/server/src/seed-examples.test.ts exercises the seeding path against a tmp store. No store-level test exists at the pinned commit.

j.j_sites_touched: packages/server/src/flow-id.ts (new), packages/server/src/routes.ts, packages/server/src/store.ts, packages/server/src/index.ts (CORS part - separate weakness in the same commit)
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Copy the 12-char nanoid alphabet from routes.ts:19-24 as `pattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9]{12}$'` onto the `id` params of the four /api/flows/:id routes and stop at the route layer - the traversal case 400s, but '/api/flows/does-not-exist' and every 'example-*' seeded flow also 400 and FlowStore still joins an unvalidated id into a path.

out_of_scope_notes: The same fix commit also tightens CORS (packages/server/src/index.ts:37, origin: true -> loopback-only callback at fix.diff:77-96,105): a separate weakness (permissive cross-origin access), not part of this advisory's path-traversal protection; noted, not pursued.

packages/cli/src/get.ts:23 and packages/cli/src/index.ts:383,427 interpolate a user-supplied flow id directly into a server URL without encodeURIComponent - client-side request-shaping only, no file operation; noted, not pursued.
